facts.text: Weighting strata combines measured rates for groups of conditions into an overall rate by multiplying each group's rate by its share of real operating time.
facts.quote: Weighting strata means combining the measured rate in each group of conditions (each stratum) into one overall rate by multiplying each by the share of real operating time that group represents.

facts.text: Braking-system strata are combinations of operating conditions, such as "haul road, clear day, loaded truck" or "loading area, dust, dusk".
facts.quote: For the braking system the strata are combinations such as "haul road, clear day, loaded truck" or "loading area, dust, dusk".

facts.text: The overall braking-system field rate is the sum over strata of w_i times p_i, where p_i is the detection or false-alarm rate measured in stratum i and w_i is that stratum's share of real exposure, such as operating hours.
facts.quote: the overall field rate as the sum over strata of w_i times p_i, where p_i is the detection or false-alarm rate measured in stratum i and w_i is that stratum's share of real exposure, for example its share of operating hours.

facts.text: Uncertainty in braking-system field-exposure weights w_i must be reported alongside the overall field rate; a precise stratum rate p_i multiplied by a guessed exposure weight w_i remains a guess.
facts.quote: The uncertainty in w_i must be reported next to the rate: how often is there really dense dust at dusk? A precise p_i multiplied by a guessed w_i is a guess [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Exposure data for off-road sites were not found in public sources.
facts.quote: Exposure data for off-road sites were not found in public sources.

facts.text: The identified routes for obtaining off-road site exposure data are customer telematics, logs of the existing warning system and site studies.
facts.quote: The only routes are customer telematics, the logs of the existing warning system and site studies

facts.text: The booklet recommends ingesting years of existing warning-system logs now and classifying them into encounter types, strata and machine configurations to obtain field-exposure weights.
facts.quote: the booklet urges ingesting years of warning-system logs now and classifying them into encounter types, strata and machine configurations [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Without good field-exposure weights, aggregate real-world detection claims have an uncertain basis; Chapter 9 identifies this as an open uncertainty.
facts.quote: Without good field weights, any aggregate "real-world" detection claim has an uncertain basis, which Chapter 9 lists as an open uncertainty.

facts.text: Field-exposure weights drift as sites, attachments and practices change, so the booklet treats the test campaign as the start of a living evidence base.
facts.quote: The weights also drift as sites, attachments and practices change, so the booklet treats the campaign as the start of a living evidence base [Chapter 9].
